title: Extension by zero base change
statement:
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ of
schemes and a Cartesian
square with base change $a:Z'\to Z$, extension by zero
([def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]) is exact and

$$
a^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!a_U^{-1}F
$$

for every sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$, and the same holds for complexes.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.70.5, [Tag `03S6`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03S6).*)

proof.text: Use the existing additive instance for openImmersionLowerShriek, the existing preservesFiniteLimits_openImmersionLowerShriek theorem, and preservation of finite colimits by the left adjoint openImmersionLowerShriek. Specialize all three to AddCommGrpCat. These give the three exactness conjuncts.

source.place: openImmersionLowerShriek_additive, preservesFiniteLimits_openImmersionLowerShriek, and the IsLeftAdjoint instance from openImmersionLowerShriekAdjunction; Stacks 03DJ and 03S5

proof.text: Apply isIso_openImmersionLowerShriekBaseChangeMap with coefficient category AddCommGrpCat directly to (IsPullback.of_hasPullback a j).flip. This proves invertibility of precisely the canonical mate appearing in the fourth conjunct, without a change of coefficient category or a specialization of module sheaves over the integers. Its inverse has the direction displayed in the blueprint.

Regard the canonical mate as a natural isomorphism using asIso and apply Mathlib NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex with ComplexShape.up integers. Its hom is definitionally the degreewise map in the fifth conjunct, so its isIso_hom proves that conjunct. The construction checks commutation with differentials by naturality and constructs the inverse degreewise. There is no boundedness hypothesis. Combine these five results by conjunction introduction.

source.place: NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex, lifting a natural isomorphism degreewise

blueprint_update.statement:
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ of
schemes and a Cartesian
square with base change $a:Z'\to Z$, extension by zero
([def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]) is exact and

$$
a^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!a_U^{-1}F
$$

for every sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$, and the same holds for complexes.

proof.text:
Extension by zero is computed sectionwise as in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]: for etale $V\to Z'$ the sections
of $j'_!a_U^{-1}F$ over $V$ are the sections of $a_U^{-1}F$ over
$V\times_{Z'}U'$, i.e. over $V\times_ZU$, while
$(a^{-1}j_!F)(V)=j_!F(V\times_ZZ_V)$ has the same description; the
Cartesian identification gives the natural isomorphism, and for
complexes the same argument applies termwise.
